bull.b: The sharp FY2026 recovery shows substantial earnings power and strong conversion of profits into cash. This provides resources for technology investment, capacity expansion and shareholder returns, although sustaining the improvement through the memory cycle remains important.

Long-term NBMs materially improve revenue visibility compared with spot memory sales and deepen strategic ties with large customers. Their growing share of bits should support planning, utilization and cash generation across several years, while financial guarantees add contractual support.

The shift toward datacenter and AI-related storage expands exposure to a faster-growing, strategically important end market. Product advances in density, power efficiency and high-bandwidth flash can strengthen SanDisk’s competitive position and support mix improvement over time.

bear.b: The move from multi-year losses to exceptional FY2026 profitability demonstrates meaningful sensitivity to memory pricing and demand cycles. If industry conditions weaken, earnings, margins and cash generation could contract sharply, making current results less durable than their scale suggests.

Weakness in PCs and smartphones reduces contribution from established consumer channels and leaves the portfolio more dependent on datacenter growth. A recovery expected only in 2027 indicates this pressure may persist through the next several months and affect mix and utilization.

Large multi-year contracts improve visibility but also concentrate revenue and bargaining exposure among fewer customers. Changes in a major partner’s demand, product plans or execution could therefore have an outsized effect on SanDisk’s growth, capacity planning and financial results.
